desc:
prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. You may make as many transactions as you like; a transaction is one purchase of a single share followed by a sale on a strictly later day. You can hold at most one share at a time, and you may sell and buy again on the same day. Every sale costs fee.

A share may not be kept too long: if you buy on day b, you must sell it on some day s with b < s ≤ b + d. Return the maximum total profit after fees (at least 0, since you may choose not to trade).

Example: prices = [1,2,3,4,5], fee = 1. With d = 4 the answer is 3 (one trade from 1 to 5). With d = 2 it is 2 (1 to 3 and 3 to 5, one fee each), and with d = 1 it is 0 (every one-day trade earns 1 - 1).
hints: Let f[i] be the best profit using days up to i with no share held at the end of day i. A sale on day i uses a purchase on a day j in a window just before i.
The purchase day j must satisfy i - d ≤ j ≤ i - 1, and the value of buying on day j is f[j] - prices[j]. You need the maximum of that quantity over a sliding window.

Maintain the window maximum with a monotonic deque of day indices holding decreasing values of g[j] = f[j] - prices[j]. Then f[i] = max(f[i-1], prices[i] - fee + g[front]), and afterwards push day i with g[i].
editorial: Without a fee the holding limit would be harmless: a long trade can always be cut into one-day trades that earn the same. The fee is what makes long holds valuable and the limit d a real restriction.

Let f[i] be the best profit after day i with nothing held. Either nothing happens (f[i-1]) or a share is sold on day i: prices[i] - fee + g[j] for the best purchase day j in [i-d, i-1], where g[j] = f[j] - prices[j] (you were flat with profit f[j] and then paid prices[j]).

Scanning the window costs O(d) per day, O(n d) overall. Because the window slides one step per day and only its maximum is needed, a monotonic deque gives amortised O(1) per day: drop indices smaller than i - d from the front before querying; after computing g[i] pop from the back every index whose g is not larger, then append i. Query before inserting day i, because the purchase must be strictly earlier. Total O(n) time and O(n) memory.
solution:
from collections import deque


def maxProfitFeeMaxHold(prices, d, fee):
    n = len(prices)
    f = [0] * n
    g = [0] * n
    dq = deque()
    for i in range(n):
        while dq and dq[0] < i - d:
            dq.popleft()
        f[i] = f[i - 1] if i else 0
        if dq:
            f[i] = max(f[i], prices[i] - fee + g[dq[0]])
        g[i] = f[i] - prices[i]
        while dq and g[dq[-1]] <= g[i]:
            dq.pop()
        dq.append(i)
    return f[n - 1]
